subject: Contract cadence orchestration & staged uptake playbook

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@acmeai.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract cadence orchestration & staged uptake playbook

Hi Elaine,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on our usage signals and your ACME Q4 roadmap, I sketched a coordinated renewal that balances predictability and flexibility: a 24-month commitment with a staged quarterly ramp and an auto-renew opt-in for year 3. The goals are to give you predictable unit pricing early (for budgeting) while preserving burst capacity and a safety buffer for peak launches.

Key bullets:
- Term: 24 months with optional auto-renew (customer-controlled opt-in at 90 days before term end)
- Staged uptake: Q1 base commit (60%), Q2 +15%, Q3 +15%, Q4 +10% to cover product launch peaks
- Co-terming: align to ACME calendar; prorated first partial period to sync invoices
- Billing: monthly with an annual true-up and an escape clause if usage drops below 40% of committed tokens for two consecutive quarters

I've attached a capacity plan (acme_capacity_plan_q4-q6.xlsx) and a first-pass amendment (redwood_amendment_draft_v2.pdf) for your procurement/legal to review. If this structure looks reasonable, Jordan and I can produce a DocuSign-ready amendment and a simple one-page rollout schedule for your ops team.

Proposed next steps:
1) ACME procurement confirms preferred cadence for invoices and any required PO flow (we can co-term or keep separate invoicing for pilot projects)
2) Redwood to deliver signed amendment (DocuSign) + onboarding ramp checklist (for launch day +30,+90,+180)
3) Finance to confirm proration approach and any required credit holds

Would you be available for a short 30-minute sync on Monday 09/28 to finalize the cadence?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the thoughtful proposal. A couple quick clarifying Qs from procurement/legal before we book time:
1) Can you confirm the exact invoicing frequency and whether we can aggregate multiple product lines onto a single monthly invoice?
2) How will the true-up mechanics work if we hit surge usage for one of our launches — is there a buffer so we don't spike over committed units and immediately incur overage rates?
3) Our legal team will want to review the auto-renew opt-in language — can you send the specific clause you propose?

We'll loop in the product launch lead (cc: jason@acmeai.com) if we move forward. Monday 9/28 at 10am PT should work for a short sync.

—Elaine
VP Product, Acme AI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@acmeai.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract cadence orchestration & staged uptake playbook

Elaine — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and commitments from our side: 

- Invoicing: We can provide a single consolidated monthly invoice that covers all Redwood products. If ACME prefers separate lines for pilot vs. production, we can model that in the amortization schedule.

- True-up / surge buffer: Proposed operational guardrails: a rolling 14-day burst buffer applied at 150% of committed throughput. Any sustained consumption beyond the buffer (30+ days above threshold) triggers a tiered overage rate or an accelerated true-up to convert burst into committed capacity. We included the detailed mechanics in section 3 of the attached amendment.

- Auto-renew clause: See clause 5.a in the draft amendment (attached). We propose customer opt-in to auto-renew at least 90 days before the renewal window; default is non-auto-renew if no action is taken. happy to adjust.

I've attached the amendment for review (redwood_amendment_draft_v2.pdf) and a brief amortization table in the spreadsheet. Jordan

Hi all —

Reviewed the draft amendment and the proposed billing cadence. A few finance-side notes: 

- Proration: For the first partial period (to co-term to ACME calendar) we will prorate by days and apply any agreed-on onboarding credits as a line item.
- Annual true-up: We'll do a 30-day notice true-up window after each 12-month mark; overages convert to invoice line items at the agreed tiered rates.
- Credit hold: We can hold an operational credit (retainer) equivalent to 5% of the annual committed spend to cover short-term flares instead of immediate invoicing, provided accounting has a PO and payment terms are net 30.

Open question for product/ops: can we agree on a definition for "sustained surge" (Jordan suggested 30+ days at 150%) so billing can be automated? If so, we'll bake that into the amendment and the billing runbook.

If procurement confirms PO workflow, I can sign off from finance and we can route the amendment to DocuSign.

Thanks,

Hey Elaine / team —

Wanted to add the operations view so expectations are clear once the amendment is live. Proposed staged onboarding timeline: 
- Day 0–30: baseline provisioning + runbook handoff (50% of Q1 committed capacity live)
- Day 31–90: scale to 80% of Q1 committed capacity, training + latency validation
- Day 91–180: full Q1 commit reached and enable burst buffer; activate additional nodes for launch week as needed

Fallback / rollback: if latency or error rates exceed thresholds during ramp, we will pause further capacity increases and engage a joint incident bridge. We recommend a one-week launch buffer where ACME can request a temporary 20% capacity increase at the burst rate without triggering an immediate contract true-up — counts against the 14-day rolling buffer Jordan mentioned.

I'll prepare a one-pager onboarding checklist and ops SLA summary and drop it in the Drive link Naomi shared.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

All —

Thanks for the fast responses and the clear asks. To summarize agreement and next actions before our 9/28 10am PT sync: 
1) Invoicing: single consolidated monthly invoice (finance to confirm PO sync) — Marissa will confirm PO/credit hold flows.
2) Surge buffer & true-up: 14-day rolling buffer at 150% with sustained surge defined as 30+ days above threshold. Finance will automate billing rules for that definition.
3) Auto-renew language: default non-auto-renew; customer must opt in 90 days prior to renewal window. Legal to propose final wording.
4) Onboarding timeline: Camila will provide the one-pager ops checklist and SLA.
5) DocuSign: Jordan and I will prepare a DocuSign package including the amendment and the onboarding checklist. We'll send the link to procurement once Marissa confirms PO lines.

If that captures it, I'll proceed to convert the draft amendment into a DocuSign-ready packet and set up the 9/28 calendar invite.
